messages.subject: Character substitution in list
parts:
Dear All,

I have 2 questions:

1- I would need to substitute a character chain in list such as:

library(plyr)
library(stringr)
nom <- structure(list(ast = structure(list(lbtest = "ast", lborresu =
"U/L",
lbornrlo = 0, lbornrhi = 37), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu",
"lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"),
alt = structure(list(lbtest = "alt", lborresu = "U/L", lbornrlo =
0,
lbornrhi = 47), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu", "lbornrlo",
"lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"), alcphos =
structure(list(
lbtest = "alkaline phosphatase", lborresu = "U/L", lbornrlo =
40,
lbornrhi = 135), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu", "lbornrlo",
"lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"), bili =
structure(list(
lbtest = "total bilirubin", lborresu = "umol/L", lbornrlo =
0,
lbornrhi = 19), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu", "lbornrlo",
"lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"), chol =
structure(list(
lbtest = "cholesterol, total", lborresu = "mmol/L", lbornrlo =
0,
lbornrhi = 5.17), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu",
"lbornrlo",
"lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"), ldl =
structure(list(
lbtest = "ldl-cholesterol", lborresu = "mmol/L", lbornrlo =
NA_real_,
lbornrhi = NA_real_), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu",
"lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame"),
hdl = structure(list(lbtest = "hdl - cholesterol", lborresu =
"mmol/L",
lbornrlo = NA_real_, lbornrhi = NA_real_), .Names =
c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
trigli = structure(list(lbtest = "triglycerides", lborresu = "mmol/
L",
lbornrlo = NA_real_, lbornrhi = NA_real_), .Names =
c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
creat = structure(list(lbtest = c("creatinine", "creatinine"
), lborresu = c("umol/L", "umol/L"), lbornrlo = c(53, 44),
lbornrhi = c(124, 89)), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu",
"lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = c(1L, 20L), class =
"data.frame"),
pot = structure(list(lbtest = "potassium", lborresu = "mmol/L",
lbornrlo = 3.6, lbornrhi = 5.2), .Names = c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
wbc = structure(list(lbtest = "wbc", lborresu = "x10^9/L",
lbornrlo = 3.5, lbornrhi = 11.1), .Names = c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
plt = structure(list(lbtest = "platelets", lborresu = "x10^9/L",
lbornrlo = 150, lbornrhi = 400), .Names = c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
urea = structure(list(lbtest = "urea (bun)", lborresu = "mmol/L",
lbornrlo = 3.2, lbornrhi = 8.6), .Names = c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
ggt = structure(list(lbtest = c("gamma gt", "gamma gt"),
lborresu = c("U/L", "U/L"), lbornrlo = c(0, 0), lbornrhi =
c(51,
33)), .Names = c("lbtest", "lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"
), row.names = c(1L, 20L), class = "data.frame"), gluc =
structure(list(
lbtest = "glucose, fasting, plasma", lborresu = "mmol/L",
lbornrlo = 3.9, lbornrhi = 6.2), .Names = c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = 1L, class =
"data.frame"),
hemog = structure(list(lbtest = c("hgb", "hgb"), lborresu = c("g/
dL",
"g/dL"), lbornrlo = c(13.2, 11.5), lbornrhi = c(17, 15.5)), .Names
= c("lbtest",
"lborresu", "lbornrlo", "lbornrhi"), row.names = c(1L, 20L
), class = "data.frame")), .Names = c("ast", "alt", "alcphos",
"bili", "chol", "ldl", "hdl", "trigli", "creat", "pot", "wbc",
"plt", "urea", "ggt", "gluc", "hemog"))

I have tried:
llply(as.list(names(nom)),function(name) nom[[name]]$lborresu <-
str_replace_all(nom[[name]]$lborresu, "x10^9/L", "x10**9/L"))

Which obviously does not give what I need, ie the same list but with
the substitution done.

2- How can I just keep the first row of all the dataframes in the list
or the last ?

Thanks for any help,

Best wishes, JL

messages.author: f03c91905cbdb6f9
messages.subject: Re: Character substitution in list
parts:
try this:

nom <- lapply(nom, function(.df){
.df$lborresu <- sub("\\^", "**", .df$lborresu)
.df
})

Here is what some of the output looks like:

$pot
lbtest lborresu lbornrlo lbornrhi
1 potassium mmol/L 3.6 5.2

$wbc
lbtest lborresu lbornrlo lbornrhi
1 wbc x10**9/L 3.5 11.1

$plt
lbtest lborresu lbornrlo lbornrhi
1 platelets x10**9/L 150 400
